correctness.rationale: Rooted three-state DP partitions each child-root condition exactly; base heights 1, 2, 3 are reconstructed and three cost/count phases are verified algebraically by induction, with explicit minimizers. The formulas reconstruct every minimum dominating set, not merely a lower bound. A leaf parent with at least two pendant children is forced in every minimum set; this proves invariance under all permitted simultaneous deletions. Reducing one sibling group to one child gives an exact two-to-one swap mapping, with the parent of the affected support vertex still dominated by another forced sibling. A graph-based standalone program checks 25 full trees, 75 stable prunings, 25 threshold cases, and 18 brute-force minimality/count instances, including nine explicit all-minimum-set classifications. Experiments corroborate, and are not relied on as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 binary-tree dominion theorem motivates asking whether bounded optimal-solution diversity and boundary perturbation behavior persist with increased branching. The result answers this for every height and branching degree, classifies ALL optimum configurations, and identifies a sharp qualitative branching transition: up to \((d-2)d^{h-1}\) leaves can be deleted without changing ANY optimum, whereas making a single bottom sibling group have only one remaining child exactly doubles the count. This is a natural structural stability threshold for a hierarchical graph family, rather than a single arbitrary small enumeration. The known binary subcase and local leaf-exchange rule are not independently claimed as novel.
